paper_type_evidence.quote: We present ALMA continuum and spectral line data at 0.89 mm and 3.2 mm for three disks surrounding young brown dwarfs and very low mass stars in the Taurus star forming region.

question.value: What are the sizes, dust structure and grain sizes of disks around three young brown dwarfs/very low mass stars in Taurus, and what do they imply for BD formation and planet formation?

evidence.quote: We analyze the continuum visibilities and constrain the disks physical structure in dust.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00259.S.

bands.value: Band 7 (~338 GHz, 0.89 mm) and Band 3 (~93 GHz, 3.2 mm), Cycle 0

evidence.quote: using ALMA Early Science in Cycle 0 at Band 7 and 3 (about 338 and 93 GHz, respectively)

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 4 spectral windows, 1.875 GHz each, 0.488 MHz channels; Band 7 centered 331.102, 332.998, 343.102, 344.998 GHz; Band 3 86.102, 87.998, 98.103, 99.998 GHz

evidence.quote: Spectral windows were centered at 331.102, 332.998, 343.102, 344.998 GHz for Band 7 observations and 86.102, 87.998, 98.103, 99.998 GHz for Band 3.
The only line emission detected was the CO ($J=3-2$) rotational line in Band 7 for 2M0444 and CIDA 1.
All observations were performed with either 25 or 26 antennas in the Extended array configuration
which provides projected baseline lengths up to $\sim$400 m

analysis_steps.goal: Measure continuum fluxes and spectral index

method.value: Integrate surface brightness of pixels with emission in natural-weighted maps; alpha from 338 and 93 GHz fluxes

evidence.quote: obtained by integrating the surface brightness from each pixel with emission

validation.value: Uncertainties include map noise and 10% flux scale

evidence.quote: the reported uncertainties account for both the noise level in the maps and the $10\%$ uncertainty on the determination of the absolute flux scale

method.value: Moment 0 and 1 maps of CO(3-2); P.A. from axis joining blue- to red-shifted pixels; inclination ranges from maps

evidence.quote: the P.A. of the disk was estimated from the angle of the axis joining the blue-shifted pixels to the red-shifted pixels in the moment 1 maps

analysis_steps.goal: Fit Band 7 visibilities with disk models

method.value: Two-layer flared disk models; surface density power law; model visibilities via Fourier transform compared at observed (u,v); chi2 with MCMC

evidence.quote: We used a Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) to run large collections of disk models by varying the input parameters that our analysis aims to constrain.

key_parameters.value: R_in = 0.05 AU; free parameters M_disk (Sigma_10AU), p, R_out

evidence.quote: For the disk inner radius $R_{\rm{in}}$ we considered a value of 0.05 AU

key_parameters.value: Grain size distribution n(a) ∝ a^3, amin 0.1 micron; T_ext = 10 K (5, 15 K tested); T ∝ R^-3/4 beyond R_thin

evidence.quote: We chose a fiducial value for $T_{\rm{ext}} = 10$ K

assumptions.value: Distance 140 pc; gas-to-dust ratio 100; kappa 0.02 cm2/g_gas at 0.89 mm

evidence.quote: The ISM-like value of 100 for the gas-to-dust mass ratio is also assumed.

fitting.value: chi2 minimization with MCMC; 1 sigma confidence intervals

evidence.quote: Intervals for each parameter are given at the $1\sigma$ confidence level.

validation.value: Best-fit model visibilities compared with binned data; T_ext variations give consistent results

evidence.quote: found best fit models with parameters which lie within the confidence intervals obtained in the 10 K case
